reading.body:
Digital Realty Northern Virginia IAD44 is a 648,500 square foot building in Sterling that is part of the largest colocation campus in Northern Virginia, a region concentrating multiple named facilities across Ashburn, Loudoun, Sterling, Reston, Bristow, and Fairfax. The operator publishes 2N+2 cooling redundancy for the building but does not publish the megawatts of power available to tenants, which limits assessment of its AI relevance to its footprint and redundancy tier alone.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 publish power capacity. Because IAD44 does not publish megawatts, it cannot be ranked within the state's published capacity and does not appear in the 1375.4 MW of disclosed Virginia capacity. This gap is typical; most facilities in the state disclose nothing.

Without published power, IAD44 cannot be directly compared to disclosed AI training builds elsewhere, and its standing in the state is unknown. Its size and redundancy suggest it is built for high-density colocation. Whether it matters to AI scaling depends on whether the operator has published capacity for other buildings in the Northern Virginia campus, which can be assessed facility by facility.
